cmes.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source may be related to a C2.0 flare and eruption from Active Region 14578 (S12W61) seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-11-17T04:51Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source longitude.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery, and to the north in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided and related to a filament eruption visible over the northeast limb in SDO AIA 171/304 and GOES SUVI 171/284/304 imagery starting around 2026-11-17T06:20Z. An opening of field lines is visible over the northeast limb at this time in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 171/284 imagery as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is an M1.1 flare and eruption from Active Region 14578 (S12W68) seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-11-17T15:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source longitude.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the NW in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-11-17T19:53Z. It is also seen to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 but is covered by a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source is likely far-sided and possibly related to some very faint field line movement seen well beyond the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 around 2026-11-17T18:00Z. A far-sided source is consistent with triangulated measurements.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

cmes.note: Narrow CME first seen to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 starting around 2026-11-17T20:30Z. It is also seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2 but is covered by a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source is likely related to a filament eruption from AR 14579 (N15E36) beginning around 2026-11-17T19:01Z best seen in SDO AIA 304. The ejecta appears to be directed northeastward.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 as well as on visible source location.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the W in GOES CCOR-1 starting at 2026-11-17T22:30Z. It is covered by real-time data gaps in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source of this CME is likely associated with an M1.7 class flare from 14578 (S12W71) which peaked at 2026-11-17T21:39Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131 accompanied by some westward directed ejecta best seen in SDO AIA 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on probable source location.

cmes.note: Narrow CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and faintly in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is not clearly seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery and may be obscured by a data gap from 2026-11-17T20:53Z to 2026-11-18T02:38Z. The source is not clear but may be an eruption beyond the NE limb as seen from SDO and GOES. An eruption starting around 2026-11-18T01:40Z can be seen beyond the east limb in GOES SUVI 304 imagery, but timing-wise this may not be the best candidate source.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

cmes.note: CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME may also be faintly visible to the NW in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is a filament eruption centered around N10W80. The eruption starts around 2026-11-18T00:52Z as seen as moving field lines near the west limb in GOES SUVI 284/304 and SDO AIA 193 imagery. Post-eruption dimming can also be seen in STEREO A EUV 195 following a data gap from 2026-11-17T21:05Z to 2026-11-18T01:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the potential source location as well as the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmes.note: Narrow CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is not found in available EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the SW in STEREO A COR2 after a data gap from 2026-11-18T07:53Z to 2026-11-18T11:09Z. The source may be part of the eruption seen near disk center in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery, potentially centered around S05W90 starting around 2026-11-18T03:55Z with moving field lines and minor dimming observed.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2. The CME front is notably distorted in the COR2 field-of-view, as such the fit encompasses the matching width from CCOR-1 and tracks the edges of the front in COR2, finding a good fit around W80-W90, better closer to W90.

cmes.note: Faint CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-18T16:00Z. This CME fades before exiting the field-of-view in C2 and is there for not visible in other coronagraphs. The source of this event is a small filament eruption seen originating from Active Region 14581 (S10E56) beginning at approx. 20206-11-18T10:54Z as seen as dimming and field line opening in SDO AIA 193.
generalNoteKeywords: Faint event; may affect type assignment

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the SW by GOES CCOR-1 beginning at 2026-11-18T21:15Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2 due to a data gap from 2026-11-18T19:00Z to 2026-11-18T23:12Z, or STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-11-18T16:38Z. The source of this event is likely beyond the SW limb and can be seen as field line movement/opening in SDO AIA 171 beginning at approx. 2026-11-18T19:48Z.

cmes.note: CME seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is also visible to the NW in STEREO A COR2 after a data gap from 2026-11-18T16:38Z to 2026-11-19T02:09Z. The source of this event is a slow erupting prominence seen originating from beyond the West limb in GOES SUVI and STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery. This prominence begins to become unstable at approximately 2026-11-18T04:15Z, but does not appear to fully erupt from the disk until approximately 2026-11-18T18:44Z. Field line opening can also be seen in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the potential far-sided source location as well as the best fit between GOES CCOR-1, SOHO LASCO C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

cmes.note: CME seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME can also be faintly seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 before a real-time data gap starting at 2026-11-19T09:48Z. The source is likely an eruption from west of Active Region 14579, located around N15E10, starting at 2026-11-19T07:09Z as seen in SDO AIA 304/193 imagery. Dimming can be best seen in SDO AIA 193 and an ejecta of material is visible in SDO AIA 304. The eruption is also visible near the east limb from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 195/304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source location as well as the best fit between STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is visible in 3 frames of SOHO LASCO C2 imagery and 2 frames of GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The majority of the measurement is using STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-11-22T03:48Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and in a single, late frame in STEREO A COR2. The majority of the CME is missed in STEREO A COR2 due to a real-time data gap. There are two notable features of this CME - a bright, narrow, bulk-like feature and a faint, wide, shock-like feature. The fainter shock feature is only seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME may be related to field line movement beyond the ENE limb in GOES SUVI 284 beginning around 2026-11-22T02:40Z. If this beyond-limb activity is the source of this CME, then there is some significant westward deflection based on triangulated measurements.
generalNoteKeywords: Likely deflection of the event within the FOV

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of narrower, brighter, bulk-like feature based only on coronagraph triangulation using SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The best source candidate is beyond the E limb.
Plane-of-sky measurement of wider, fainter, shock-like feature based only on using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. This feature is not seen in STEREO A COR2.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-11-22T07:48Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. There are two notable features to this CME - a narrower, brighter, bulk-like feature and a wider, fainter, shock-like feature. There is not a good source candidate for this CME on the Earth-facing disk, so the source may be far-sided with a significant amount of deflection.
